decisions.reason: As a core safety-shoe line that became more prominently presented in 2024, it fits the firm's strongest existing knowledge base and looks like a product the firm can continue refining and selling profitably.
The comfort insole is closely related to the firm's footwear and fitting capabilities, but its limited prominence suggests it is more of a supporting range item than a strategic growth product.

The supportive insole also builds on the firm's footwear and foot-support knowledge, yet its unchanged low visibility and overlap with other insole offers make it somewhat more vulnerable to portfolio cleanup.
An ergonomic safety-shoe series is highly consistent with the firm's innovation path, core technical know-how, and customer demand for better fit and workplace comfort, so it is very likely to stay.

Firefighter and rescue boots are adjacent to the firm's established protective-footwear competences and gained visibility in 2024, indicating that the firm has learned enough from the launch to keep developing the segment.

As a homepage-featured flagship with explicit evidence of customer use, the moulded insole clearly matches the firm's absorptive capacity in foot measurement and custom solutions and is extremely unlikely to be withdrawn.
